newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: N.Zealand winter festival begins-without snow.
newsitem.headline: N.Zealand winter festival begins-without snow.

text.p: The southern hemisphere's biggest winter festival kicked off in New Zealand's skiing mecca of Queenstown on Saturday with a colourful street parade and multitudes of tourists -- but no snow.

The picturesque resort town, nestled beside Lake Wakatipu in the craggy peaks of New Zealand's South Island, has drawn thousands of visitors to its 23rd annual winter celebrations heralding the start of the ski season.
Only the weather has failed to come to the party.
Just a limited part of one of the four major ski fields in the area is open for business, thanks to snow-making machines.
But festival organisers remain undaunted and are predicting a bumper ski season.
"Snow is one of those things, it comes when it decides to come -- sometimes sooner, sometimes later," said Duncan Smith, operations manager for Mount Cook Ski Areas.
"The winter festival is a celebration of the start of winter, to show the season is under way. It's a time to enjoy and have fun."
More than 60 events have been organised for the nine-day festival. Highlights include the launch of a new bungy jump off a peak 400 meters above the township by bungy pioneers AJ Hackett Bungy.
Queenstown attracts about 650,000 visitors a year, of which 450,000 are overseas tourists. About 15,000 people are expected to visit Queenstown this week alone for the winter festival.

Festival organiser Vaughan Schwass said tourists were attracted to Queenstown by the wide variety of leisure and adventure activities available, many of which are not available in one setting elsewhere.

"We don't get huge numbers of international visitors travelling here necessarily to ski. Here you can ski in the morning and play golf in the afternoon, which is quite a novelty for a lot of North American visitors," he said.
Other Queenstown attractions include jetboating, white water rafting, skydiving, paraponting, nature walks, outback safaris and helicopter excursions, to name but a few.
New Zealand Tourism Board statistics show 1.55 million international visitors came to New Zealand in the year to March, 1997. Tourism is New Zealand's single largest export earner.
